chapter: Kansas City, Omaha and Lloyd Hunter
title: Firing Lloyd Hunter after the Pipestone gig
summary: At Pipestone, Minnesota the band got drunk on spiked ice water, and the angry young Gus fired leader Lloyd Hunter.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Like, as we were talking about that, I was playing bass in the band. And we left and went to Pipestone, Minnesota. I think that was Minnesota. Yeah, it was, Pipestone, Minnesota.
And we played out in some field, like, where everybody came in from different -- little towns.

And it was hot. And so this guy brought up a bucket of water with ice in it, and then came and poured a whole gallon of just straight alcohol in there. And they began to drink that alcohol and that water, and they got drunk. I'm playing the bass, and the band began to sound bad, because they were missing notes and couldn't play their horns.
And I got mad, and I started cussing out Lloyd Hunter and all of the guys that was drunk. And I

And I told them, him, and everybody else they were fired. And I fired Lloyd, the leader of the band, that night. And he said, 'Okay, well, I'll just take my horn and go.' And he packed his horn up and walked out the door, and got outside, and it struck him that that was his band, and I fired him. And he came back in and said, 'You can't fire me, I'm the leader of this band.' I was the youngest thing in the band, really. And I fired him. And then he came back in, they finished their gig, and he started thinking about it. He said, 'You fired me out of my band. I've never had nobody to fire me out of my band.'
